description: Syscalls hard-blocked in the merged hardened profile even where both Docker's and Podman's defaults allow them (typically behind a capability gate). These stay blocked no matter what capabilities a container is later granted (e.g. via --cap-add), removing the capability grant as a way to unlock them. See ANALYSIS.md for full rationale and references.

syscalls.name: ptrace
syscalls.reason: Process-introspection primitive used to read/inject into sibling processes and steal credentials; blocking it regardless of CAP_SYS_PTRACE stops a debug-capability grant from doubling as an attack primitive.

syscalls.name: process_vm_readv
syscalls.reason: Same class of risk as ptrace: reads another process's memory directly. Blocked regardless of CAP_SYS_PTRACE.

syscalls.name: process_vm_writev
syscalls.reason: Same class of risk as ptrace: writes another process's memory directly. Blocked regardless of CAP_SYS_PTRACE.

syscalls.name: perf_event_open
syscalls.reason: Recurring source of Linux kernel privilege-escalation CVEs and a common Spectre-class side-channel primitive. Gated by CAP_SYS_ADMIN/CAP_PERFMON upstream; blocked outright here.

syscalls.name: bpf
syscalls.reason: The BPF verifier has been a repeated source of container-escape and kernel LPE vulnerabilities. Gated by CAP_SYS_ADMIN/CAP_BPF upstream; blocked outright here.

syscalls.name: userfaultfd
syscalls.reason: Used as a race-condition/heap-grooming timing primitive in numerous public kernel-exploit proofs of concept. Podman allows it completely ungated by default.

syscalls.name: keyctl
syscalls.reason: Kernel keyring manipulation, implicated in past kernel privilege-escalation CVEs (e.g. CVE-2016-0728). Already excluded by the intersection since Docker never allows it; listed explicitly as a floor against upstream drift.

syscalls.name: add_key
syscalls.reason: Kernel keyring manipulation; same rationale as keyctl. Already excluded by intersection; listed as an explicit floor.

syscalls.name: request_key
syscalls.reason: Kernel keyring manipulation; same rationale as keyctl. Already excluded by intersection; listed as an explicit floor.

syscalls.name: mount
syscalls.reason: Mount manipulation is central to most container-breakout techniques. Ordinary application containers never need to call this themselves; the runtime handles mounts before the workload starts.

syscalls.name: umount2
syscalls.reason: Same rationale as mount: unmounting from inside the container is a breakout/tamper primitive, not an application need.

syscalls.name: pivot_root
syscalls.reason: Root-filesystem-switching primitive used in container-escape chains; no legitimate use inside an already-running application container.

syscalls.name: unshare
syscalls.reason: Namespace manipulation used to create new, less-confined namespaces from inside the container; a building block of several breakout techniques.

syscalls.name: setns
syscalls.reason: Namespace manipulation: lets a process join another namespace, another building block of breakout techniques.

syscalls.name: kexec_load
syscalls.reason: Loads a new kernel to be executed on reboot; no legitimate use in an application container and a severe host-compromise primitive if reachable.

syscalls.name: kexec_file_load
syscalls.reason: File-based variant of kexec_load; same rationale.

syscalls.name: reboot
syscalls.reason: Host/system power-management syscall with no legitimate use inside an application container.

syscalls.name: acct
syscalls.reason: Enables/disables kernel process accounting; a system-administration syscall with no legitimate use inside an application container.

syscalls.name: swapon
syscalls.reason: Swap-space management is a host-level concern; Podman allows it completely ungated by default.

syscalls.name: swapoff
syscalls.reason: Swap-space management is a host-level concern; Podman allows it completely ungated by default.

syscalls.name: nfsservctl
syscalls.reason: Legacy in-kernel NFS server control interface, removed from modern kernels; no legitimate use in a container and a bare attack surface if present.

syscalls.name: uselib
syscalls.reason: Obsolete shared-library-loading syscall with no legitimate modern use and a history of being a hardening target.

syscalls.name: vm86
syscalls.reason: Legacy x86 virtual-8086 mode syscall with no legitimate use in a container workload.

syscalls.name: vm86old
syscalls.reason: Legacy x86 virtual-8086 mode syscall with no legitimate use in a container workload.

syscalls.name: query_module
syscalls.reason: Kernel module introspection; module syscalls have no legitimate use in an application container.

syscalls.name: init_module
syscalls.reason: Loads a kernel module; a direct host-compromise primitive with no legitimate use in an application container.

syscalls.name: delete_module
syscalls.reason: Unloads a kernel module; no legitimate use in an application container.

syscalls.name: finit_module
syscalls.reason: File-descriptor-based variant of init_module; same rationale.

syscalls.name: iopl
syscalls.reason: Grants direct I/O port access; a hardware-level primitive with no legitimate use in an application container.

syscalls.name: ioperm
syscalls.reason: Grants direct I/O port access; a hardware-level primitive with no legitimate use in an application container.
